what_its_for: Levobunolol is an eye drop used to lower pressure inside your eye. It is used to treat glaucoma and a condition called ocular hypertension (high eye pressure). Lowering eye pressure helps protect your vision and prevents damage to your optic nerve.
how_to_take: Use this medicine only in your eye — never swallow it. Wash your hands before and after using the drops. Tilt your head back, pull down your lower eyelid to make a small pocket, and place one drop into that pocket. Close your eye gently for 1 to 2 minutes and press lightly on the inner corner of your eye (near your nose) with your finger. This helps keep the medicine in your eye and reduces absorption into your body. Do not let the dropper tip touch your eye, finger, or any surface. If you wear contact lenses, remove them before using the drops and wait at least 15 minutes before putting them back in.
dosing: The usual dose is 1 drop in the affected eye(s) once or twice daily, as directed by your doctor. The 0.5% strength is typically used once a day, and the 0.25% strength may be used twice a day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not use two doses at the same time to make up for the one you missed.
storage: Store levobunolol eye drops at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Do not freeze the drops. Keep the medicine out of direct sunlight and away from heat. Keep all medicines out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid touching the dropper tip to any surface, including your eye or hands, to prevent contamination. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery right after using the drops until your vision clears, as you may have temporary blurry vision. Avoid wearing contact lenses during treatment unless your doctor says it is okay. Tell your doctor before using any other eye drops or eye medicines, as you may need to space them apart by at least 5 to 10 minutes. Avoid using this medicine if you have certain heart or breathing problems unless your doctor has specifically approved it.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: shortness of breath or wheezing, slow or irregular heartbeat, chest pain or tightness, sudden vision changes, severe eye pain, redness, or swelling, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing, feeling faint or very dizzy, unusual tiredness or weakness, or depression or mood changes. Also let your doctor know if your eye pressure does not seem to be getting better.
when_it_works: Levobunolol usually begins to lower eye pressure within 1 hour of using the drop. The full pressure-lowering effect is typically reached within a few hours. You may not feel any different because high eye pressure usually has no symptoms, but your doctor will check your eye pressure at follow-up visits to make sure the medicine is working.
special_populations: Older adults may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medicine, especially effects on the heart and lungs. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before using this medicine, as it may affect your baby. This medicine should be used with extra caution if you have asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), heart failure, slow heart rate, or diabetes, as it may hide the warning signs of low blood sugar or worsen breathing problems. Always tell your doctor about all your medical conditions and all the medicines you take, including vitamins and supplements.
